data.one_liner: A fast Dart implementation of the k-dimensional (k-d) tree data structure.
data.what_it_does: Organizes points in a k-dimensional space to enable fast spatial searches, nearest neighbor lookups, and range queries. It allows inserting, removing, and querying points efficiently using a custom distance function.
use_when: You need to perform nearest neighbor or range searches on multidimensional spatial data.
You are working with coordinate data that benefits from space-partitioning trees.
avoid_when: You only need simple one-dimensional collections or standard lists.
Your dataset changes constantly and you need heavily optimized self-balancing mechanisms without rebuilding.
strengths: Super fast Dart implementation of the k-d tree algorithm.
Supports nearest neighbor queries with optional maximal search distance.
Includes JSON serialization and balance factor approximation.
weaknesses: Unreliable balance factor for small trees.
No built-in alternative packages from the catalog to compare against.
